title: Boss: the gateway
summary: Put applications, subscriptions, scopes, rate limits and a product together in one gateway model.

steps.title: The brief
body: You are modelling Acme's gateway before configuring the real product, so the team agrees on exactly what every
consumer will see. The model takes a request and answers like the real gateway would.

steps.title: Route by context and version
prompt: The tests declare `record Published(string Context, string Version, string Method, string Template, string? Scope, string Endpoint);`, one per published operation.
Write `(int Status, Published? Op) Find(List<Published> apis, string method, string path)`:
- the path must start with `/{context}/{version}/`; the rest is matched against the operation's template (`{x}` matches one non-empty segment; literals ignore case; equal segment counts);
- an operation matching method (ignore case) and template → `(200, op)`;
- template matched under that context/version but not the method → `(405, null)`;
- nothing matched → `(404, null)`.
starter: (int Status, Published? Op) Find(List<Published> apis, string method, string path)
solution: (int Status, Published? Op) Find(List<Published> apis, string method, string path)
if (segs.Length < 2 || !string.Equals(segs[0], api.Context, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || segs[1] != api.Version) continue;
for (int i = 0; i < t.Length && ok; i++)
if (!(t[i].StartsWith("{") && t[i].EndsWith("}")) && !string.Equals(t[i], rest[i], StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) ok = false;
hints: Split the path once; check context and version before matching the rest.
template: record Published(string Context, string Version, string Method, string Template, string? Scope, string Endpoint);

steps.title: The whole gateway
prompt: The tests declare `Published` (as before), `IClock`/`FakeClock`, and give you `Router.Find` (in your editor).
Write a class `Gateway`:
- `Gateway(List<Published> apis, IClock clock)`;
- `void AddToken(string token, string app, params string[] scopes)`: register an issued token;

- `void Subscribe(string app, string context, string version, int perMinute)`: subscribe an app to one API version with a plan of `perMinute` calls (a token bucket with capacity `perMinute` and rate `perMinute / 60.0` per second, one bucket per app and API version);
- `(int Status, string? Endpoint, string? RetryAfter) Handle(string method, string path, string? authorization)`:
1. `Router.Find` the operation → 404 / 405 as found (before any token checks: unknown paths are 404 for everyone);
2. `Bearer <token>` must be a registered token → else `401`;
3. the token's app must be subscribed to that context/version → else `403`;
4. the operation's scope (if any) must be among the token's scopes → else `403`;
5. the bucket must have a token → else `429` with `RetryAfter` = seconds as a string;
6. otherwise `(200, op.Endpoint, null)`.

readonly Dictionary<string, (string App, string[] Scopes)> tokens = new();
readonly Dictionary<(string App, string Context, string Version), Bucket> subscriptions = new();
public void AddToken(string token, string app, params string[] scopes) => tokens[token] = (app, scopes);
public void Subscribe(string app, string context, string version, int perMinute) =>
subscriptions[(app, context, version)] = new Bucket { Capacity = perMinute, Rate = perMinute / 60.0, Tokens = perMinute, Last = clock.NowMs };
public (int Status, string? Endpoint, string? RetryAfter) Handle(string method, string path, string? authorization)
if (op is null) return (status, null, null);
if (authorization is null || !authorization.StartsWith("Bearer ") || !tokens.TryGetValue(authorization[7..], out var t))
if (!subscriptions.TryGetValue((t.App, op.Context, op.Version), out var bucket)) return (403, null, null);
hints: Follow the six steps in order, returning as soon as one fails.
Key the buckets by `(app, context, version)`; refill exactly like the token bucket lesson.
template: Dojo.Eq("unknown path is 404 even without a token", 404, dojoGw.Handle("GET", "/nope/v1/x", null).Status);
Dojo.Eq("subscribed but missing scope -> 403", 403, dojoGw.Handle("POST", "/orders/v1/orders", "Bearer t-report").Status);
Dojo.Eq("allowed -> forwarded to the endpoint", (200, "http://orders-integration:8080", (string?)null), dojoGw.Handle("POST", "/orders/v1/orders", "Bearer t-shop"));
Dojo.Eq("report call 3 -> 429, retry after 30 s", (429, (string?)null, "30"), dojoGw.Handle("GET", "/catalogue/v1/books/1", "Bearer t-report"));
Dojo.Eq("limits are per app: shop still fine", 200, dojoGw.Handle("GET", "/catalogue/v1/books/1", "Bearer t-shop").Status);
Dojo.Eq("after 30 s report may call again", 200, dojoGw.Handle("GET", "/catalogue/v1/books/1", "Bearer t-report").Status);
record Published(string Context, string Version, string Method, string Template, string? Scope, string Endpoint);
public long NowMs { get; private set; }
public void Advance(int ms) => NowMs += ms;

steps.title: Who needs a bigger plan?
prompt: The gateway's log gives `(string App, int Status)` per call. Write `List<string> Review(List<(string App, int Status)> log)`
returning one line per application, sorted by name (ordinal):
`"{app}: {n} calls, {t}% throttled, {d}% denied"` where throttled = `429`, denied = `401` or `403`, percentages rounded **down** to whole numbers.
Then append, in this order:
- `" -> upgrade plan"` if throttled is at least 20%;
- `" -> check credentials"` if denied is at least 50%.
starter: List<string> Review(List<(string App, int Status)> log)
solution: List<string> Review(List<(string App, int Status)> log)
foreach (var g in log.GroupBy(e => e.App).OrderBy(g => g.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal))
var d = g.Count(e => e.Status is 401 or 403) * 100 / n;
hints: `GroupBy(e => e.App)`, then count inside each group.
template: var dojoLog = new List<(string App, int Status)>();
Dojo.Eq("an empty log", new List<string>(), Review(new()));
